findings.title: long_marginal: the blend and the pool it is subtracted from still live in different universes (the candidate's own NaNs are not aligned)
findings.summary: The blend is NaN wherever the candidate is NaN (steer.py:432), but the pool book it is differenced against is built on every tradable name and cached once per context (steer.py:445-446), so a candidate's coverage alone moves its own equal-weight benchmark and the measured 'marginal' is not a marginal. pool_in_universe() fixed only the untradable half of exactly this bug; its own docstring states the principle it still violates ('Both sides of the difference must live in the same universe').
findings.failure_scenario: Candidate = a literal copy of the known pool panel, NaN on the 10% of names with the lowest average return (run_mining passes min_coverage=0.9, so this is the most NaN the GP's own gate allows). It adds exactly zero information: inside its universe the blend's ranking IS the pool's ranking. reward(..., 'long_marginal') returns score -0.972 (train -0.972 / valid -0.367). The same difference with the pool restricted to the cells where the blend exists returns exactly +0.000 / +0.000. The bias grows monotonically with missing coverage (2% -> -0.274, 5% -> -0.484, 10% -> -0.972, 20% -> -1.763) and its sign flips with which names are missing (+0.717 when the missing names are the HIGH-return half), so it is a per-candidate bias that reorders candidates, not an offset. THR for this reward is 0.2, so the bias is up to 5-9x the discovery threshold. episodes/e1_I2_dispersion_fold/evidence.json has all 160 candidates in both arms at score -0.62..-3.03 with sign<0 for 100% of them -- the same range and sign this bug produces.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the blend's universe the pool's universe instead of the candidate's, so the cached pool rows stay valid: `sm = np.where(np.isfinite(pu), np.where(np.isfinite(z), 0.5 * z + 0.5 * pu, pu), np.nan)` -- a missing candidate value then means 'no tilt' rather than 'drop the name'. (The alternative, recomputing ctx._pool_rows per candidate on `np.where(np.isfinite(sm), pu, np.nan)`, is correct too but defeats the cache and doubles the cost of every long_marginal evaluation.)
findings.evidence: Repro: /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/review/reward-math/t2d_coverage_sweep.py (coverage sweep, printed above), /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/review/reward-math/t2c_marginal_universe.py (realistic-turnover pool: implementation -3.348, same-universe control +0.000), t2b_marginal_universe.py (opposite sign: +0.717 vs +0.000). findings.title: fit = 0.03 x score is signed and centred on zero, and AlphaCube's cluster cull uses a cutoff relative to |best|
findings.summary: long_marginal and long_screen return a DIFFERENCE, so fit straddles zero. AlphaCube's cull_clusters computes `cutoff = best - 0.5 * abs(best)` (src/alphacube/mining/clustering.py:102), which was written for a fitness bounded below by 0 (|rank_ic| - 0.14*turnover, 99th pct ~0.03). When best is near zero the survivor band collapses to nothing and the GP breeds from a single cluster; when best is negative the band is 0.5*|best| wide and culls far more than intended.
findings.failure_scenario: Fitness vector [0.0, -0.0226, -0.0290, -0.0340, -0.0374, -0.0410, -0.0451, -0.0500] (the 0.0 is the no-op screen of the next finding; the negatives are e1's actually observed fits): best=0.0 -> cutoff=0.0 -> cull_clusters empties 7 of 8 clusters, so from that generation on _next_generation breeds only from the no-op and the remaining budget produces nothing. With e1's control-arm fits alone (all negative, -0.0226..-0.0451) only 2 of 6 clusters survive, versus 4 of 6 for AlphaCube's own positive fitness on the same spread. gp_params in idea_search.py:262 does not pass cull_rel_threshold, so the 0.5 default is in force.
findings.suggested_fix: Offset the fitness so it is positive over the working range of the differenced rewards, e.g. `fit = 0.03 * (r["score"] + 3.0)` for long_marginal/long_screen (keeping 0.03 x score for the level rewards), and keep the un-offset value in p_score for the THR gate. Alternatively pass `cull_rel_threshold` through gp_params, but a relative band cannot be made safe across zero.
findings.evidence: /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/review/reward-math/t4_bucket_screen_scale.py section D, plus the direct best=0.0 check printed above. Fit distribution read from episodes/e1_I2_dispersion_fold/evidence.json.

findings.title: long_screen is baselined against the UNSCREENED known family while the already-screened version is in the pool list, and the pool de-duplication is skipped for this reward
findings.summary: base = G.spec['pool'][0] = known_amt_dispersion (unscreened), while long_marginal's pool = G.spec['pool'][-1] = known_xfrozen, which is literally that family with a frozen-quote screen already applied. So a long_screen candidate is paid the full known -> known_xfrozen gain for rediscovering a result the batch already has, and idea_search.py:330 exempts long_screen from the rho_pool/rho_known >= 0.5 filter, so the rediscovery is also counted in independent_distinct / efficiency_per_100 -- the headline of the steer-vs-control protocol (E6).
findings.failure_scenario: guidance/B01.yaml: known_xfrozen = `cs_last_high20(neg(cross_mean(day_std(Amt),30)), cross_max(day_zero_ratio(Ret),15))`, and cs_last_high20(y,x) is documented as 'rank(y) with the highest 20% of x placed below every other stock' -- i.e. exactly the long_screen transform at steer.py:435 with candidate = `cross_max(day_zero_ratio(Ret),15)`, which is idea I1's seed #1 verbatim. The guidance's own evidence line records that step as train pure-long Sharpe 2.22 -> 3.15, so that seed scores ~+0.93 against THR=0.2, passes, survives the (skipped) de-duplication, and is reported as a 'distinct passer outside the known pool'. Because seeds bypass the guidance filter (idea_search.py:214) and only the steer arm gets seeds, the steer arm's efficiency_per_100 is inflated by at least one guaranteed known passer that the control arm cannot get for free -- so the episode would report the intervention as more efficient regardless of whether it is.
findings.suggested_fix: For long_screen pass `base = pool_sig` (the last pool entry, known_xfrozen) instead of known_z, so a rediscovery of the frozen screen scores ~0; or, if the unscreened base is deliberate, keep it but drop the `KIND != "long_screen"` exemption at idea_search.py:330 and add known_xfrozen's traded signal to the rho comparison set so rediscoveries are excluded from the headline count.
findings.evidence: guidance/B01.yaml pool[0]/pool[1] and ideas.I1_frozen_state.seeds; partura/ops_ext.py:346-350 (cs_last_high20 docstring); scripts/idea_search.py:102, 214, 330.

findings.title: long_screen's z > 0.3 is not 'the candidate's top two tenths' on a saturating panel, and one direction can screen nobody and score exactly 0.000
findings.summary: _zrank averages ties, so a large tie block gets one z and the 0.3 cut is all-or-nothing for the whole block. Idea I1's grammar is built entirely from saturating occupancy ratios (day_zero_ratio / day_flat_ratio / day_flat_run_max / day_at_max_ratio / day_at_min_ratio), which is exactly the panel shape that breaks the cut. Worse, when the floor block is the majority, the inverted direction puts it at an averaged rank below 0.3 and nothing is screened at all: the reward then returns the base's own score, i.e. score exactly 0.000, which competes in the (sign, hl) argmax against real measurements and wins whenever every genuine screen hurts on train.
findings.failure_scenario: Candidate panel = an occupancy ratio with 66% of cells at the floor and ~11 distinct values a day (what day_zero_ratio(Ret) looks like; distinct_fraction is not the binding gate here). z>0.3 screens 26.81% of names at hl=0 but 20.00% at hl=5 and hl=20, so the (sign, hl) grid picks hl=0 (train +1.375) over hl=20 (train +1.357) partly because it screens 7 percentage points deeper -- half-life is confounded with screen depth and r['hl'] does not mean what it says. In the same run, (sign=-1, hl=0) screens 0.00% of names and returns score exactly +0.000 / +0.000; had the positive direction been harmful on train, the grid would have returned that no-op as the candidate's score, which is finite, enters the archive at fit = 0.0, and then triggers the cluster collapse in the finding above. Candidate coverage also silently rescales the depth: with 20% of names NaN the screen removes 16.76% of the base universe, not 20%.
findings.suggested_fix: Cut by count rather than by the z value: per day take the top ceil(0.2 * n_finite) by rank with an explicit deterministic tie rule (or push the whole straddling tie block out and record it), so the screened fraction is 20% by construction. Additionally reject a (sign, hl) whose screened fraction falls outside, say, [0.10, 0.30] instead of letting a 0%-screen no-op win the argmax, and return the realised screened fraction in the reward dict so it can be checked.

findings.title: The untradable mask is applied to the raw panel BEFORE the EMA, so it changes the signal's value and not just the universe
findings.summary: reward() masks `raw` and then smooths it, so ema_rows is fed only the unmasked days and the realised half-life is longer than the grid point and different for every name. book_row already drops NaN-signal names from both the book and the benchmark (books.py:61-65), so masking AFTER the EMA gives the identical tradable universe with an undistorted half-life. The flag is a daily top-20% cross-sectional cut (idea_search.py:100), i.e. 20% of cells, and names move in and out of it.
findings.failure_scenario: A 20%-of-cells mask that flips about 4 times a year per name, hl=20: mask-then-EMA (as implemented) gives train pure-long Sharpe +7.418 / ann +45.77% / turnover 2.5%, while EMA-then-mask on the identical universe gives +7.802 / +47.92% / 2.9%. A reported 'best half-life 20' is really an effective ~25 and name-dependent, so two candidates whose untradable patterns differ are compared at different effective half-lives (R6's 'fix the half-life when comparing structures' is not actually held fixed), and any ann quoted from long_tradable / long_bucket / long_marginal is ~2pp low.
findings.suggested_fix: Smooth first, mask second: `sm0 = bk.smoothed(np.asarray(panel, float), hl)` and apply `np.where(ctx.untradable, np.nan, ...)` to sm0 (once, outside the sign loop, since the mask commutes with the sign flip).
findings.evidence: /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/review/reward-math/t3_mask_before_ema.py (output above; mean daily rank correlation between the two signals 0.9978 at hl=20 -- small per-cell but it moves the chosen half-life and the quoted ann).

findings.title: An unrecognised reward kind silently runs the unmasked `long` reward and records the wrong name
findings.summary: reward() dispatches on `kind` with no else branch and no membership check against REWARDS, and idea_search.py:65 takes KIND straight from the command line or the YAML `reward:` field without validating it. Any typo produces a plausible number computed under the plain `long` convention, and the reward dict and evidence.json record the typo'd string as if it had been honoured.
findings.failure_scenario: `--reward long_tradeable` (or a `reward: long_tradeable` in guidance/<batch>.yaml): reward() skips the untradable mask at steer.py:421 and every elif, so it scores the unmasked `long` book. On a 20%-untradable synthetic panel the real long_tradable score is -3.329 while the typo returns -0.214 -- identical to `long` to 15 digits, a 3.1-Sharpe difference -- and the result carries kind='long_tradeable'. idea_search.py:68 also silently uses THR=1.0 for a misspelled 'long_screen'/'long_marginal' instead of 0.2, so the episode's pass count is computed against the wrong threshold as well. Nothing in evidence.json records that the named reward was never run.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `if kind not in REWARDS: raise ValueError(f"unknown reward kind {kind!r}; expected one of {REWARDS}")` at the top of reward(), and validate KIND against partura.steer.REWARDS in idea_search.py right after it is parsed.
findings.evidence: Verified inline (output above): kinds 'long_tradeable', 'LONG_TRADABLE', 'long_bucket_rank' and '' all return without error and all give exactly the `long` score.

checked_and_fine: RewardContext.__init__ was truncated when pool_in_universe was inserted: `self.halflives`, `self._bucket` and `self._pool_rows` had become dead code after the method's `return`, so every reward() call raised AttributeError: 'RewardContext' object has no attribute 'halflives' and the halflives= kwarg was silently dropped. ANOTHER AGENT FIXED THIS AT 19:34 DURING THIS REVIEW and I re-verified all five kinds now run (tmp/review/reward-math/t1_ctx_attrs.py). No artefact is void: episodes/*/evidence.json are 17:15 and 18:34, both before the 19:27 breakage. Residual, unfixed hazard worth one line of work: scripts/idea_search.py:272 catches the exception from run_mining and writes evidence.json with no error field, so a crashed arm is recorded as scored~1 / archive 0 / passers 0 -- indistinguishable in the machine-readable artefact from 'the idea genuinely found nothing'.

No look-ahead anywhere in the context or the books. cross_mean / cross_max / cross_valid_count go through rolling_windows (AlphaCube src/alphacube/operators/common.py:426), documented and implemented as causal trailing windows left-padded with NaN; ema_rows is a causal per-stock EMA; _zrank is purely within-day; untradable's `possible = np.minimum(241, np.arange(1, len(dates)+1))` uses only days the view has already seen; PanelSet.target(1) row t is the t->t+1 label with the t+1 limit-up lock applied back to row t, and book_row pairs signal row t with target row t. idea_search opens only 20180102-20230807, so the holdout is untouched.

Direction and half-life are chosen on train only, exactly as R5/R6 say: the grid's argmax key is book_row(sm, ctx.tgt, ctx.train)['long_sharpe'], the valid book is built once afterwards at the kept (sign, hl), and score = min(train, valid) with both_periods defaulting to True (R4). The argmax is deterministic (strict `>`, so the first maximum in hl-ascending / sign=+1-first order wins), and selecting by the raw train Sharpe rather than by the difference is equivalent because base_tr is constant across the grid for both long_marginal and long_screen.

_bucket_rank is numerically sound: output is in (0, 1] within each bucket, a NaN signal gives NaN out, a NaN liquidity key (bucket -1) gives NaN out, and an empty bucket neither crashes nor shifts anyone -- because non-finite cells are relabelled to the overflow bucket n, `cnt` counts only the finite members of each real bucket, so `within/cnt` is the rank among tradable names in that bucket. Ties inside a bucket are broken by column (symbol) order via the stable lexsort, which is unavoidable here and is guarded upstream by the distinct_fraction >= 0.5 gate. Verified: tmp/review/reward-math/t4_bucket_screen_scale.py section A.

long_bucket really is liquidity-tilt-neutral, which is the whole point of R2. With bucket populations made deliberately unequal by concentrating the untradable mask in the lowest-liquidity names (36.5 vs 35.2 eligible names per bucket), the pooled top decile still takes 9.8-10.0% of every bucket's eligible names, so the book's bucket weights match the equal-weight benchmark's and no bucket-level return difference leaks into the excess. Verified: t4_bucket_screen_scale.py section B.

long_screen's two sides share one stock pool and one benchmark: the screened signal and ctx.base are finite on exactly the same cells (both are `np.where(np.isfinite(ctx.base), ..., np.nan)`), so long_book's `ok = isfinite(sig) & isfinite(target)` selects the same names on both sides and the equal-weight benchmark does not move. The screened block's values, -1.0 + 0.1*base, lie in [-1.05, -0.95], strictly below the unscreened range [-0.5, 0.5], and preserve the base's own order among the screened names.

long_screen being excluded from the untradable mask is deliberate, not an oversight: guidance/B01.yaml's note on idea I1 states that the tradable-pool reward would pre-remove the very thing the idea is looking for. It is also self-consistent, because ctx.base (known_z) is unmasked too, so the difference is still measured inside one universe. Separately, known_z is correctly left unsmoothed: G.spec['pool'][0]['hl'] is 0, so the base book matches that family's published convention.

pool_in_universe's caching is safe for what it does cache -- the untradable mask is fixed for the life of a RewardContext, so re-ranking the pool once is correct. The defect is only that the candidate-dependent part of the universe cannot be handled by a once-per-context cache (first finding).

ParturaScorer.__init__ (scripts/idea_search.py:132) refuses to run unless the GP's label grid matches ctx.tgt in both shape and finite pattern, so the reward context cannot silently drift out of alignment with the panels the search scores.

books.py's convention that a held name with a missing label earns 0 while its weight still counts, and is excluded from the equal-weight benchmark, is the user's published convention (documented at books.py:8-11) and is applied identically to both sides of every reward, so it does not create an asymmetry between a candidate book and its base.
